responsibilities: Meridian are hiring a BI Analytics Engineer to enable high‑value analytics and decision‑making by designing and maintaining trusted, analytics‑ready data models that translate business questions into reusable, reliable data assets and support scalable, self‑service analytics across Meridian.
We’re looking for someone who can consult with the business to build a strategic enterprise view of how to deliver data modelling across domains.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: designing and maintaining trusted, analytics‑ready data models that translate business questions into reusable, reliable data assets
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Trust and reliability carry the role summary; the single "thrives in a fast-paced environment" sits in a culture-fit bullet, not the work.
evidence.domain_risk: our two brands, Meridian and Powershop retail electricity to more than 400,000 homes, businesses and farms across New Zealand
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: A large utility retailer, but the JD frames the output as decision support with no financial-reporting, audit or regulatory language.
evidence.collaboration_width: No distinctly named partner teams — only "the business" and "cross-functional delivery teams".
evidence.data_team_maturity: Strong experience developing and operating analytics models on a cloud data platform (e.g. Databricks, Snowflake, Fabric).
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A platform and a self-service analytics audience already exist, but no named sub-teams or scale signals place it beyond growing.
evidence.jd_authorship: enable high‑value analytics and decision‑making by designing and maintaining trusted, analytics‑ready data models
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The role summary is abstract while the skills list is precise (Kimball, Data Vault, OBT, Delta Live Tables) — specificity sits in requirements, not the work description.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: support scalable, self‑service analytics across Meridian
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The audience is downstream analytics consumers served through a semantic layer, not one business function.
evidence.autonomy_level: consult with the business to build a strategic enterprise view of how to deliver data modelling across domains
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role is asked to set the enterprise-wide approach to data modelling, not to deliver against someone else's scope.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: AI is not mentioned anywhere in the posting.
evidence.testing_framing: No testing or data quality signal anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: "Trusted" and "reliable" appear as adjectives on the data models, with no testing tool or quality practice named.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The JD is written entirely in enablement terms — no incidents, no compliance, no cost of getting it wrong.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: designing and maintaining trusted, analytics‑ready data models
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Design and build sit alongside maintaining an existing estate, with neither dominant.
evidence.work_arrangement: We value work/life balance, so our flexible work options (where possible) make things easier for you and your whānau.
